tools.xax_build: JVM snapshot build preview: byte-stages the current host-authorized, already-resolved canonical snapshot into owned work scratch and invokes the exact JVM-capable native XAX compiler's build command. Native build verifies the complete snapshot and emits an executable JAR and provenance; no canonical parsing, workload computation, Java source generation, javac, Python compiler or interpreter is on the request path. Unresolved request roots decline in this profile. Returns the current canonical root, actual artifact byte count and provenance bytes/hex. This separate JVM preview uses its own immutable tested compiler manifest while the default deployment pin stays unchanged. package/entry selection, result handles and toolchain caching remain unsupported. Native exact-root XAXEDIT1 mutations of unsigned resolved JVM memory-profile snapshots are supported through the separately pinned tested compiler. The native editor rebuilds the reachable package, request and snapshot, then mandatory verification precedes publication. Signed-package changes, recursion-group users, signature/provenance rewriting and unresolved requests remain outside this mutation profile.
tools.xax_construct: Construct a new supported graph with an exact-root XAXEDIT1 typed mutation carrier. Native XAX applies and verifies the staged candidate before publication. The record is hexadecimal transport; canonical semantic state is source. JSON xax-construct-v1 is unsupported. Native exact-root XAXEDIT1 mutations of unsigned resolved JVM memory-profile snapshots are supported through the separately pinned tested compiler. The native editor rebuilds the reachable package, request and snapshot, then mandatory verification precedes publication. Signed-package changes, recursion-group users, signature/provenance rewriting and unresolved requests remain outside this mutation profile.
tools.xax_execute: JVM executable-JAR preview on Windows: stages only the current authorized resolved canonical snapshot and invokes the exact host-granted native XAX compiler's build command, then the native XAX launcher starts the host-selected Java 17 runtime inside a Windows AppContainer and one-process job. Requires --allow-execute and host-owned XAX_MCP_JAVA. Clients cannot choose the runtime, class path, JAR, executable, file path, environment, JVM options, grants or larger budgets. Optional stdin_hex supplies at most 262144 exact binary bytes followed by physical EOF. args excludes argv[0], is limited to 64 strings and 8192 UTF-16 units, and is passed after the fixed -jar artifact to generated JVM main; the XAX JVM process entry has no startup-argument readers. Arguments must fit Windows-1252; @file/-version stay literal. Other characters decline. Fixed VM options enable class verification, cap Java heap at 64 MiB, bound VM caches, disable attach/performance data and use one active processor. The native job enforces five seconds total CPU, ten seconds wall time, one process, 256 MiB process commit and 1 MiB combined returned output. The child receives OS-derived SystemRoot and container-local LOCALAPPDATA; Java option/classpath environment variables are not inherited. The owned JAR alone gets an AppContainer read grant, restored during normal cleanup. Returns separate exact stream hex, raw process exit, measured wall/user/kernel CPU, peak process commit and stdin_bytes_supplied. Native setup, measurement, budget and cleanup failures fail closed; Java exceptions and Java-heap exhaustion are raw child exits and stderr, not separately classified traps. This profile is device-independent JVM classfile major 61, tested with canonical JVM memory-profile snapshots and Microsoft OpenJDK 17 on Windows. unresolved build requests, JVM startup reads, JNI/registered external tools, other runtimes and cross-platform launchers are not certified. Workspace content integrity, atomic publication, crash/pressure/escape acceptance and promotion remain open. Native exact-root XAXEDIT1 mutations of unsigned resolved JVM memory-profile snapshots are supported through the separately pinned tested compiler. The native editor rebuilds the reachable package, request and snapshot, then mandatory verification precedes publication. Signed-package changes, recursion-group users, signature/provenance rewriting and unresolved requests remain outside this mutation profile.
